newsitem.title: UK: LucasVarity sights 280 mln stg pretax in yr.
newsitem.headline: LucasVarity sights 280 mln stg pretax in yr.

text.p: Anglo-U.S. auto components and engineering group LucasVarity Plc on Tuesday described as "realistic" recent estimates that it should make proforma pretax profits of about 280 million pounds in the year to January 31.

In a trading statement and update on the progress being made to integrate the former Lucas Industries Plc and Varity Corp, merged last year, the group said it was encouraged by the wider outlook and was "optimistic that significant overall growth can be achieved in 1997."

The group said that, after accounting changes related to the merger, it expected its gearing ratio (indicating the ratio of its debt to its equity capital) to be in the 70 percent-plus range at the end of its current year.

It said it then saw gearing "dropping rapidly by the end of next year, due to strong underlying cash flow, progress on working capital reduction and the proceeds from the disposal programme announced last December".

As the group aims to pay a dividend for the period ending January 31 this year of 2.1 pence, the board sought to clarify its view of future distribution policy, which it has said would be based on a mixture of dividends and share buy-backs.

"The board would not likely consider a future reduction in the dividend without announcing a share repurchase programme. In any event, the company will seek the views of our major shareholders prior to any decision," it explained.

LucasVarity shares built on their earlier gains after the trading update was released, and by 1525 GMT they stood up a net 12 pence on the day at 217-1/2 pence in robust turnover of over five million shares. ($1=.6199 Pound)
